newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Mitsui chemical firms consider merging.
newsitem.headline: Two Mitsui chemical firms consider merging.

text.p: Two Japanese chemical companies in the Mitsui conglomerate's stable said on Monday they were considering merging next year, a move which could make the new firm the second-largest petrochemical company in the country.

While the firms said talks were continuing, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Monday that Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd had already decided to merge into a new firm.

Mitsui Toatsu, the fifth-largest petrochemical maker in Japan, makes resins and various petrochemical products and Mitsui Petrochemical, the seventh largest, is a leading maker of materials for plastics and synthetic textiles.

"We are considering a merger with Mitsui Toatsu as early as October 1997. But at this moment, the matter is still undecided," Mitsui Petrochemical president Shigenori Koda said in a statement on Monday.
Mitsui Toatsu president Akio Sato also released a statement in which he basically reiterated Koda's comments.
Parent sales of the new company, expected to be called Mitsui Chemical, would be about 700 billion yen ($6.42 billion) in the first business year, the newspaper said.
The merger was decided to increase the two companies' international competitiveness, it said.

Mitsui Toatsu would be dissolved on the merger. It said 0.5 to 0.6 Mitsui Petrochemical shares would be exchanged for one Mitsui Toatsu share, it said. The new company would produce materials for plastics, fertilisers, pharmaceutical products, electronics products and other petrochemical products, it said.

Mitsubishi Chemical Corp is Japan's top chemical company and would remain the industry leader even if the merger between Mitsui Petrochemical and Mitsui Toatsu takes place, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Mitsubishi Chemical was launched in October 1994 through a merger between two chemical firms in the Mitsubishi group, another major conglomerate in Japan. ($1=109 yen)
